subject: c12-math
scope: CBSE Class XII Mathematics (041) 2026–27 written/theory Board-exam preparation; internal assessment excluded.
note: Official CBSE 2026-27 theory unit marks: Relations and Functions 8, Algebra 10, Calculus 35, Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry 14, Linear Programming 5, Probability 8; total 80, internal assessment 20.

reference.label: Relations and Functions — Tip 1
reference.text: Check domain, codomain and range before deciding whether a function is one-one or onto.

reference.label: Relations and Functions — Tip 2
reference.text: Use the definition f(x1)=f(x2) => x1=x2 for one-one proofs.

reference.label: Relations and Functions — Tip 3
reference.text: For composition, verify that the output of the inner function lies in the domain of the outer function.

reference.label: Relations and Functions — Tip 4
reference.text: Do not assume an inverse exists; the function must be bijective for an inverse function.

reference.label: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Tip 1
reference.text: Write the principal-value range before simplifying an inverse-trigonometric expression.

reference.label: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Tip 2
reference.text: Treat sin^-1 x, cos^-1 x and tan^-1 x as inverse functions, not reciprocals.

reference.label: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Tip 3
reference.text: Check the sign and quadrant when using inverse-trigonometric identities.

reference.label: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Tip 4
reference.text: Do not drop principal-value restrictions when converting between inverse functions.

reference.label: Matrices — Tip 1
reference.text: Check matrix orders before addition or multiplication.

reference.label: Matrices — Tip 2
reference.text: Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative: AB and BA must be treated separately.

reference.label: Matrices — Tip 3
reference.text: For an inverse, first check that the matrix is square and nonsingular.

reference.label: Matrices — Tip 4
reference.text: Keep row and column positions consistent when computing products and transposes.

reference.label: Determinants — Tip 1
reference.text: Use the correct cofactor sign pattern when expanding a determinant.

reference.label: Determinants — Tip 2
reference.text: Before using A^-1 = adj(A)/|A|, verify that |A| is non-zero.

reference.label: Determinants — Tip 3
reference.text: For area questions, take the absolute value of the determinant expression.

reference.label: Determinants — Tip 4
reference.text: When solving AX=B by inverse matrices, verify that the coefficient matrix is invertible.

reference.label: Continuity and Differentiability — Tip 1
reference.text: Check continuity using limit equals function value at the point.

reference.label: Continuity and Differentiability — Tip 2
reference.text: Choose the differentiation rule from the structure: product, quotient, chain or implicit differentiation.

reference.label: Continuity and Differentiability — Tip 3
reference.text: For inverse-trigonometric derivatives, preserve the correct denominator and sign.

reference.label: Continuity and Differentiability — Tip 4
reference.text: In parametric differentiation, divide dy/dt by dx/dt; do not differentiate as if y were directly a function of x.

reference.label: Applications of Derivatives — Tip 1
reference.text: Find critical points from f'(x)=0 and also check points where f'(x) is undefined.

reference.label: Applications of Derivatives — Tip 2
reference.text: Use sign changes of f' to establish increasing or decreasing intervals.

reference.label: Applications of Derivatives — Tip 3
reference.text: For maxima/minima, verify the required conditions rather than stopping at f'(x)=0.

reference.label: Applications of Derivatives — Tip 4
reference.text: In rate-of-change problems, define the variables and their relationship before differentiating.

reference.label: Integrals — Tip 1
reference.text: Always include +C with an indefinite integral.

reference.label: Integrals — Tip 2
reference.text: Look for substitution when the derivative of an inner expression is also present.

reference.label: Integrals — Tip 3
reference.text: Use integration by parts when the integrand is a suitable product.

reference.label: Integrals — Tip 4
reference.text: For definite integrals, apply limits after obtaining the antiderivative.

reference.label: Integrals — Tip 5
reference.text: Use even/odd symmetry and definite-integral properties before doing long calculations.

reference.label: Applications of Integrals — Tip 1
reference.text: Sketch the curves or identify their intersection points before setting up an area integral.

reference.label: Applications of Integrals — Tip 2
reference.text: Use upper minus lower when integrating with respect to x.

reference.label: Applications of Integrals — Tip 3
reference.text: Split the interval when the upper/lower curve changes.

reference.label: Applications of Integrals — Tip 4
reference.text: Use absolute area where the signed integral would otherwise cancel regions.

reference.label: Differential Equations — Tip 1
reference.text: Identify whether the differential equation is separable, homogeneous or linear before starting.

reference.label: Differential Equations — Tip 2
reference.text: For homogeneous equations, use y=vx and replace dy/dx accordingly.

reference.label: Differential Equations — Tip 3
reference.text: For dy/dx + Py = Q, calculate the integrating factor before integrating.

reference.label: Differential Equations — Tip 4
reference.text: Keep the arbitrary constant until the final step and apply any initial condition afterward.

reference.label: Vector Algebra — Tip 1
reference.text: Check vector magnitude before forming a unit vector.

reference.label: Vector Algebra — Tip 2
reference.text: Use the dot product for angles/projections and the cross product for perpendicular-area relationships.

reference.label: Vector Algebra — Tip 3
reference.text: Remember that l^2+m^2+n^2=1 for direction cosines.

reference.label: Vector Algebra — Tip 4
reference.text: Keep scalar and vector products distinct; their outputs are different types of quantities.

reference.label: Three-Dimensional Geometry — Tip 1
reference.text: Extract direction ratios carefully from the vector or Cartesian equation of a line.

reference.label: Three-Dimensional Geometry — Tip 2
reference.text: For the angle between lines, use their direction ratios.

reference.label: Three-Dimensional Geometry — Tip 3
reference.text: For skew-line distance, keep the vector order consistent in the scalar triple-product expression.

reference.label: Three-Dimensional Geometry — Tip 4
reference.text: Check whether lines are parallel, intersecting or skew before choosing the distance method.

reference.label: Linear Programming — Tip 1
reference.text: Define the decision variables before writing constraints.

reference.label: Linear Programming — Tip 2
reference.text: Translate every verbal condition into a linear inequality carefully.

reference.label: Linear Programming — Tip 3
reference.text: Include non-negativity constraints when the variables represent quantities.

reference.label: Linear Programming — Tip 4
reference.text: Evaluate the objective function at the relevant corner points of the feasible region.

reference.label: Probability — Tip 1
reference.text: Write the events clearly before applying conditional probability.

reference.label: Probability — Tip 2
reference.text: Check independence rather than assuming it from the wording.

reference.label: Probability — Tip 3
reference.text: Use total probability when the sample space is partitioned into mutually exclusive exhaustive cases.

reference.label: Probability — Tip 4
reference.text: For Bayes' theorem, identify the prior probabilities and the conditional probabilities before substituting.

mistakes: Using a formula without checking its conditions.
Sign errors in derivatives, determinants and vector calculations.
Arithmetic mistakes caused by rushing the final simplification.
Writing only the final answer in long-form questions instead of showing the required steps.
order: Start with Relations and Functions (8 marks): Relations and Functions → Inverse Trigonometric Functions.
Give the largest study block to Calculus (35 marks): Continuity and Differentiability → Applications of Derivatives → Integrals → Applications of Integrals → Differential Equations.
Then Vectors and Three-Dimensional Geometry (14 marks): Vector Algebra → Three-Dimensional Geometry.
Finish Linear Programming (5 marks) and Probability (8 marks), then revise mixed questions.
